claims.text: OpenAI News RSS timestamps publication of the Australian Youth Safety Blueprint at 12:00 UTC on 18 September 2026.
claims.sourceLocator: RSS item title, canonical link and pubDate

claims.text: The blueprint contains six pillars covering responsible adoption and literacy, privacy-protective age assurance, under-18 safety policies, manipulative interactions, crisis response and parental controls.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 launch summary; s3 PDF pages 2–6

claims.text: The blueprint is an OpenAI policy contribution rather than an enacted Australian rule or independent assessment.
claims.sourceLocator: OpenAI describes a contribution and roadmap; government source separately identifies its own exposure draft

claims.text: OpenAI says ChatGPT for Teens began rolling out in Australia in August 2026.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 paragraph 3; s3 PDF page 2; s4 launch page

claims.text: OpenAI says accounts stated or predicted to belong to 13–17-year-olds receive the teen experience and uncertain cases default to the safer experience.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 PDF pages 2–3; s4 opening and safeguards; s5 age prediction; s8 overview

claims.text: OpenAI documents stronger teen restrictions in areas including graphic violence, sexual or romantic roleplay, dangerous activities, self-harm and disordered eating.
claims.sourceLocator: s4 Stronger protections and healthy use; s5 age prediction safeguards list

claims.text: Current OpenAI help material describes ChatGPT for Teens as the same service with additional protections and says rollout and features can vary by account or region.
claims.sourceLocator: Overview, Availability and FAQ

claims.text: OpenAI says age prediction uses account and behavioural signals including account age, typical activity times, usage patterns and stated age.
claims.sourceLocator: How age prediction works

claims.text: OpenAI says an adult misclassified into the teen experience can verify through Persona, which may request a selfie, government ID or both depending on country, deletes uploaded identity material within seven days, and passes age-related information rather than the submitted image or document to OpenAI.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 PDF page 3; s5 verification paragraph; s7 verification and privacy sections

claims.text: The reviewed OpenAI materials do not publish an independent Australian error analysis for age prediction, subgroup results, appeal completion or Persona failure rates.
claims.sourceLocator: Bounded absence finding across the registered current OpenAI sources; article does not infer failure

claims.text: OpenAI parental controls require linked accounts, allow selected settings and schedules, do not let a parent read conversations, and can be unlinked by either party.
claims.sourceLocator: s6 Getting started and settings; s8 Parental controls and privacy; s14 Overview, Link your accounts, Manage parental controls and Unlink your accounts

claims.text: OpenAI describes safety notifications for linked teen accounts as limited, enabled by default, reviewed by trained staff and not a substitute for professional care or emergency services.
claims.sourceLocator: s4 default protections; s6 Notifications; s14 Safety notifications, Notification review and Manage notification preferences

claims.text: The blueprint recommends that connected parents be notified by default if a teen expresses suicidal intent, while OpenAI's current product documentation describes a narrower linked-account, detection and review workflow.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 PDF pages 4–6; s6 Notifications

claims.text: The blueprint proposes practical independent assessments under common standards and plain-language public summaries.
claims.sourceLocator: PDF page 7

claims.text: The blueprint does not specify assessor accreditation, mandatory metrics, pass thresholds or detailed access arrangements, so the value of an assessment depends on later implementation choices.
claims.sourceLocator: Bounded reading of the assessment proposal on PDF page 7; implementation consequence is Index Us synthesis

claims.text: eSafety says relevant Age-Restricted Material Codes for designated internet services, a category that includes generative AI services, commenced on 9 March 2026.
claims.sourceLocator: Covered services and commencement sections

claims.text: eSafety guidance says age-assurance methods should be tested before and during use, monitored for circumvention, demographic effects, privacy complaints and breaches, and externally audited or independently validated where appropriate.
claims.sourceLocator: PDF pages 85–90

claims.text: OAIC guidance calls for necessity and proportionality, privacy impact assessment, vendor due diligence, bias monitoring, low-intrusion alternatives, transparency, accessible review, minimisation and destruction or de-identification of age-assurance inputs when their purpose is complete.
claims.sourceLocator: Key considerations list

claims.text: The Australian Government released the Digital Duty of Care exposure draft on 8 September 2026 and set 22 September 2026 as the consultation deadline; it is not enacted law.
claims.sourceLocator: s12 publication and consultation status; s13 marked exposure draft

claims.text: The exposure draft would require in-scope providers to ensure a safe online environment so far as reasonably practicable, conduct written risk assessments, document measures and expected effectiveness, reassess at least annually and before risk-adding changes, retain assessments and provide them to eSafety on request.
claims.sourceLocator: Draft Act sections 25H, 26 and 26A; PDF pages 31–34

claims.text: Independent assessment is useful only if it tests deployed behaviour with sufficient access and publishes methods, scope, limitations and failure categories rather than checking for the existence of policies alone.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: blueprint assessment proposal, regulator testing/privacy guidance and draft effectiveness records; recommendation is Index Us synthesis

claims.text: Families and schools can check whether the teen experience and linked controls are active, but current documentation does not establish that these controls make a generative system risk-free.
claims.sourceLocator: Product availability, safeguards and OpenAI's own statement that guardrails are not foolproof; recommendation is bounded synthesis
